AITA for telling my girlfriend that I don't care about what she is talking about? | Throwaway account. Last night my girlfriend and I were hanging out on the couch. She was watching TV while I was scrolling through the news on my phone. I was in the middle of reading an article and she just started talking about stupid things (like what would happen if someone's eyeball popped out of socket) so I turned to her and said "I'm trying to read this article and I don't really care about what you're talking about." Maybe it wasn't the nicest way to put it but she was talking about something irrelevant that I honestly did not care about while I was in the middle of reading something. If she would have waited until I was finished reading I probably wouldn't have said that and just listened to her dumb stories. Well she got super pissed by my comment and said "I listen to you talk about stuff that I don't care about" then she left my house. I didn't hear from her for the rest of the night and today she is talking to me but only one or two word responses. So AITA?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: I would rate this as 1, meaning YTA (You're The Asshole). While it's understandable that you were engaged in reading an article and didn't want to be interrupted, your response to your girlfriend was dismissive and hurtful. Telling someone that you don't care about what they're talking about can be perceived as a personal rejection, implying that their thoughts and feelings are not important or interesting to you. A more considerate approach would have been to acknowledge your girlfriend's attempt to start a conversation, express your current engagement with the article, and suggest a better time to talk. For example, you could have said, "Hey, I'm in the middle of reading this article, can you give me a few minutes to finish? I'd love to hear what you're thinking about afterwards." By responding in a blunt and uncaring manner, you prioritized your own interests over your girlfriend's feelings and needs, which can damage the emotional connection and trust in your relationship. It's not about the topic being "irrelevant" or "dumb," but about showing respect and empathy towards your partner's thoughts and emotions.
